## Accepted result and published package

**An application of separable-state nonrepresentability to Grassmann orbitopes and calibrations**, Alec Kriebel, version 1.0, 12 October 2026. Published preprint and source/verification kit: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23353160 (https://zenodo.org/records/23353160).

The full existential negative resolution of the universal supporting affine-SOS assertion in Sanyal–Rostalski's OWR13/2015 problem is accepted at the exact original head `f6570e093267a7f910faf9cdd60dfbc1c12f5681`. The oriented mass ball C(4,12) has no arbitrary finite projected SDP lift: its positive complex-plane face and a PSD support equation select an ambient-linear copy of normalized complex Sep(3,3), and Fawzi's established Theorem 1 supplies the decisive obstruction. A compact full-real-ideal, size-496 moment argument then gives a failing rational unnormalized supporting functional. Its constant closed comass-one normalization has no finite pointwise or local norm completion, giving a negative answer in general to Harvey–Lawson Question 6.5.

The result is existential. No explicit failing coefficients, exact comass, rational normalized calibration, least ambient dimension or lower-dimensional classification is established. Fawzi's theorem is an established external dependency. Finite symbolic checks corroborate the algebraic bridge and do not reprove no-lift or construct the failing calibration.

## Mathematics, attribution and independent review

The root and fresh distinct geometry and SOS/source reviewers independently verified the complete scoped deductions and exact source interfaces. A fresh bounded priority audit made 84 focused queries and checked 25 primary PDF versions. Classical Kähler/Wirtinger faces and fermionic projector hulls, Vrana–Lévay's exact tensor-to-wedge lemma, theta/moment and cone-lift frameworks, and the earlier Sanyal–Rostalski equivalence are explicitly credited. Nearby quadratic Grassmann cones and unprojected-LMI obstructions are distinguished. Worldwide originality and current worldwide openness remain unestablished; no first-solution or new underlying no-lift theorem claim is made.

Four NEW independent whole-preprint/package reviews followed repair loops. The fourth reviewer rederived the entire theorem, checked primary bodies, all six paper pages, original Git tree, metadata and source archive, replayed all 48 portable executions and added 30 hostile controls. Its final verdict found **zero actionable P0–P3 issues**. Only unchanged terminal review evidence and administrative acceptance/navigation records were appended after that review; the reviewed TeX, PDF, checker, certificates, runner and metadata stayed unchanged.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, source auditing and preparing the paper. This is an unrefereed preprint with AI adversarial reviews. Conventional human peer review, journal acceptance and proof-assistant certification are not claimed.

## Preservation, portable verification and publication evidence

All 29 original files remain byte-for-byte preserved. The current portable Python 3.10+ standard-library kit executes three unchanged full symbolic baselines and 45 certificate faults, fifteen families repeated in normal/-O/-OO modes, comparing complete stdout/stderr, exit statuses and recursive JSON types. Six coordinate and nine schema/metadata fault families reject before the general projector/minor identities, which the three baselines verify. The original UID1000 environmental harness and module are historical evidence and are not imported, executed or simulated by this portable runner. Historical scripts and stage counts are not promises of current portable replay.

The final deposit has a six-page PDF (SHA256 `2228c5e4379d43302b5ca2d0f97e99d428e3755fc14abb91accef168d2b533d5`) and a 253-entry source/verification ZIP (SHA256 `d7519c53310f6a1425fcc8b521f8b6f7e2c94a372bca9bf0173ee8f047706c5d`). The repository Zenodo kit verified uploaded bytes and metadata, with only its documented paragraph-apostrophe normalization, confirmed publication and DOI HTTP200 resolution. No GitHub release was created. The exact DOI/details row is recorded through the Google Workspace CLI with read-back verification.

Two of the original five proof routes were used; no new discovery route is asserted during publication preparation. Original QUEUE and stage records remain historical; current acceptance and publication receipts are in `draft_pr_actual_claims_1000_1100_20261012/audits/pr1031_30002816`.

## Accepted scope

Problem 30002816 / OWR-13498-004: full existential negative resolution of the all-dimensional degree-at-most-one affine SOS conjecture. Two of five proof routes used; no new proof route added during publication preparation.

The full proof establishes that C(4,12), the convex hull of oriented unit simple four-vectors in R12, has no arbitrary finite projected semidefinite lift. An explicit 225-dimensional real-linear projector embedding identifies a Kähler face with the established Slater-state body. A zero-pure-block-trace section forces the individual convex summands into the mixed block and is exactly Sep(3,3). Fawzi's published Theorem 1 supplies the no-lift obstruction. Universal affine-linear SOS supporting certificates, with constants included, would instead provide a compact size-496 moment lift of trace 2.

The conclusion is stronger than nonspectrahedrality or failure of a selected hierarchy. It is an existential counterexample: a failing rational-coefficient linear form exists before comass normalization. No explicit coefficients, exact comass, minimal dimension, or lower-dimensional classification are provided. The constant closed four-form consequence addresses the Harvey–Lawson pointwise/local completion question. Fawzi's theorem remains an explicitly cited external dependency.

## Attribution and literature status

The full mathematical audit accepts the reduction. This is AI-assisted independent mathematical acceptance, not conventional human peer review or journal acceptance. Priority remains unestablished; the bounded literature review found no complete matching or contradictory primary theorem.

The established Slater-state body is credited to Schliemann–Cirac–Kuś–Lewenstein–Loss (2001), alongside classical Kähler/(p,p)-form constructions. Paul–Zhao–Dai, arXiv:2607.20623v1, Appendix A.2, use the same opposite-spin wedge isometry and a close positive-observable support-function/fidelity identity. No novelty is claimed for these components. Bettiol–Kummer–Mendes's Corollary 4.2/Remark 4.3 concerns nonnegative quadratics and the representation Sym²(Λ^k R^n), distinguished from the oriented degree-one Plücker body here.

- Fawzi: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-021-04163-2
- Schliemann et al.: https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.64.022303
- Paul–Zhao–Dai: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20623v1
- Bettiol–Kummer–Mendes: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03713v2

## Preservation and publication boundary

The full proof is included once, with an exact contextual status-only patch. The patch applies and reverses with zero fuzz and no offsets, preserving all mathematics. The full independent audit is mathematically complete with one provenance-only privacy redaction, documented without publishing the omitted provenance. Every mathematical statement, proof assessment and validation finding, including the public proof hash, remains intact. The independent read-only checker and exact 225-column certificate are byte-preserved.

Only authored mathematics, audits, acceptance material and public scholarly verification metadata are included. No copied source bodies, dataset contents, private sources, private coordination, identifying metadata for excluded private files, QUEUE changes or unrelated repository paths are included.

## Local sealed verification

The independently fixed external bootstrap pins a noncircular whole-payload manifest and exact verifier/control code. The final packet was replayed under normal, -O and -OO Python modes with -I -S -B, actual UID/EUID1000, real write denials, exact recursive inventory and unchanged before/after snapshots.

Per mode, the finite suite checks one positive independent exact algebra run and fifteen intended certificate mutants: six coordinate-matrix changes and nine certificate/schema changes. The positive run verifies all 225 embedding columns, the full Gram matrix with multiplicities 15/210, both section functionals, all 495 general-projector coordinates in 24 real variables with 11760 polynomial terms, and nine mixed minors. Each negative must fail for its exact intended reason. Complete raw stdout/stderr, exact exits, JSON types, identities, counts, reasons, categories and nested checker output are compared, without normalization or PASS filtering.

Publication controls are separate from those fifteen certificate mutations. They include fixed-bootstrap tamper/resealing tests, strict schema/scope controls, direct output-comparator attacks and hostile import environments. The actual additive diff was then applied in a fresh holdout location and the entire --controls suite rerun in all three modes. All complete raw output matched the original external controls exactly and all snapshots were unchanged.

The original writing author generator, original audit harness, historical receipt replay, excluded inventory replay, source-body/dataset replay, formal proof-assistant verification and a reproof of Fawzi's theorem are NOT_RUN by this delivery. The full audit's earlier author regenerations are historical evidence, not mislabeled as new sealed executions. The current replay uses only the immutable certificate and preserved independent standard-library checker; no SymPy import or source write occurs.

All verification in this section is pre-upload local verification. Remote byte retrieval and replay are separate subsequent checks.
